message.content:
Below is a concise overview of the key rights and protections you have as a tenant in Texas. (This is general information and not legal advice; for specific situations you may want to consult an attorney or a local tenant‑rights organization.) | Area | What the law says | Practical Tips | |------|-------------------|----------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlords may charge up to **one month’s rent** for a furnished unit and **two months’ rent** for an unfurnished unit.
• The deposit must be returned within **30 days** after you move out, minus any lawful deductions (e.g., unpaid rent, damage beyond normal wear). | • Keep a copy of the lease and a move‑in inspection checklist.
• Take photos or videos of the unit when you move in and out. | | **Habitability** | • Landlords must keep the premises in a **safe, sanitary, and livable condition** (e.g., functioning plumbing, heating, electrical, no mold, pest control).
• Texas law requires landlords to repair major defects that affect health or safety. | • Report problems in writing (email or letter) and keep a copy.
• If the landlord fails to act, you may withhold rent or repair and deduct, but do so only after following the proper notice procedures. | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease. Late fees are allowed only if the lease states them and they are reasonable (usually not more than 5% of the rent). | • Pay by check, money order, or electronic transfer and keep proof of payment. | | **Notice Requirements** | • **Month‑to‑month** tenants: 30‑day written notice to terminate.
• **Fixed‑term** leases: the lease ends automatically unless renewed; landlords must give notice if they intend to change terms. | • Provide written notice (email or letter) and keep a copy. | | **Entry Rights** | • Landlords must give **reasonable notice** (usually 24 hours) before entering, except in emergencies. | • Keep a log of any entries and verify that the notice was given. | | **Discrimination** | • Texas law (and federal Fair Housing Act) prohibits discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or other protected classes. | • If you suspect discrimination, file a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights or the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlords must follow the formal eviction process: serve a written notice (e.g., 3‑day notice for non‑payment, 30‑day notice for lease termination), file a lawsuit, and obtain a court judgment. | • Respond promptly to notices; you may negotiate a payment plan or dispute the claim in court. | | **Repair and Deduct** | • If the landlord fails to repair a major defect, you may repair it yourself and deduct the cost from your rent, but you must follow the proper notice and documentation steps. | • Keep receipts and a detailed record of the repair. | | **Lease Terms** | • The lease is a binding contract. Landlords cannot unilaterally change terms without your agreement. | • Read the lease carefully before signing; ask for clarification on any ambiguous clauses. | | **Privacy** | • Landlords cannot monitor your activities inside the unit without consent. | • If you suspect surveillance, document it and seek legal counsel. | | **Utilities** | • The lease should specify who pays utilities. If utilities are included, the landlord must maintain the service. | • Verify utility accounts and keep records of payments. | | **Subletting** | • Many leases allow subletting with landlord approval. Texas law does not prohibit subletting, but the lease may restrict it. | • Obtain written permission before subletting. | | **Maintenance of Common Areas** | • Landlords must keep common areas (hallways, elevators, parking lots) safe and clean. | • Report hazards promptly. | | **Legal Remedies** | • If your rights are violated, you can file a complaint with the Texas Attorney General’s Office, the Texas Commission on Human Rights, or the local housing authority. | • Consider mediation or small‑claims court for disputes. | ### Quick Checklist for Tenants 1. **Read the Lease** – Understand rent amount, due date, security deposit limits, pet policy, maintenance responsibilities, and notice periods. 2. **Document Everything** – Photos, videos, written notices, and receipts. 3. **Know Your Local Ordinances** – Some cities have additional tenant protections (e.g., rent control, eviction moratoriums). 4. **Keep Copies of All Correspondence** – Emails, letters, and notices from the landlord. 5. **Know When to Seek Legal Help** – If you face eviction, discrimination, or serious habitability issues. --- #### Resources - **Texas Attorney General – Consumer Protection Division**: [https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov](https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov) - **Texas Commission on Human Rights**: [https://www.tchra.org](https://www.tchra.org) - **Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs**: [https://www.tdhca.state.tx.us](https://www.tdhca.state.tx.us) - **Local Tenant‑Rights Organizations** (e.g., Texas Tenants Union, local legal aid clinics) If you have a specific situation (e.g., a notice of eviction, a dispute over a repair, or a potential discrimination claim), let me know and I can provide more tailored guidance.
